Our journey

Built by people who still train

Rawcage started because the gear in UK gyms either cost a fortune or fell apart by month three. So we picked the leather ourselves, argued about foam density, and put every prototype through real sparring before it got a name.

For the client

What changed,
and why

Six decisions behind this mockup, against the live site and the Nike / adidas / Helmetverse references.

Hero

Type off the photo, not on it

The live hero sets white text over a busy, low-contrast gym photo, so it fails contrast and the headline disappears. Nike and adidas both split: image on one side, type on a flat ground. The product actually worn in the shot is now tagged and priced, so the hero sells something.

Finder

The Helmetverse idea, applied

Boxing gloves are a sizing decision most buyers get wrong (weight vs. bodyweight vs. use). A plain-English matcher answers the question they'd otherwise ask a coach, and routes them to one product instead of a grid. It's the strongest differentiator on the page.

Product cards

Colourways, not seven listings

Seven Makari products all read "RAWCAGE [COLOUR] MAKARI COWHIDE LEATHER BOXING GLOVES", so the name is 90% duplicate. Cards now show a short name, the discipline, and a swatch row, so the range reads as one premium line.

Palette

Warm concrete, not black-on-black

Every combat brand defaults to black. Your product photography is shot on light grey seamless, so a warm neutral ground lets the gloves carry the colour, and the dark bands hit harder when they're used twice, not everywhere.

Typography

One condensed voice

Saira Condensed for display echoes the wordmark and scales to Nike-sized headlines; IBM Plex Sans and Mono handle body and data. Three roles, one system. The live theme mixes weights without a scale.

Copy

Manifesto trimmed to a claim

"Pressure builds warriors" is a strong line buried under three paragraphs. It moves to the hero as an eyebrow; the story becomes one paragraph plus three concrete pillars near the bottom, where a founder story belongs.
